events.what: Cheng & Sgueglia prove that for large even n, K_n has a 1-factorization in which (1-o(1))n of the matchings pairwise form Hamilton cycles (Thm 1.2), plus an auxiliary near-optimal construction of edge-disjoint perfect-pair matchings (Thm 1.3)
events.ai_basis: The construction in Theorem 1.3 is a generalisation of the one presented at the beginning of the Introduction and was generated by ChatGPT 5.4, which also gave a correct but rather long proof. The one presented here is a cleaner, shorter and substantially different one, and was obtained by the authors.

events.what: Glock & Sgueglia study edge-disjoint perfect-pair matchings in random graphs G(n,p)

judgement.doubts: Status progress is right: an asymptotic (1-o(1)) fraction is a bound, no n settled. The AI call hinges on reading the disclosure: 'The one presented here' most naturally refers to the proof, so the Theorem 1.3 construction printed in the paper is ChatGPT's, while its proof and all of Theorem 1.2 are human. If the authors meant the construction was also replaced, ai_role would be none. Theorem 1.3 is a result on the same bullet in the same event, so it counts under 'part of the mathematics in the result'.

corrections.why: F9: the basis quote says the construction in Theorem 1.3 'was generated by ChatGPT 5.4'; only the proof was replaced ('The one presented here is a cleaner, shorter ... one'). The AI-generated construction is part of the mathematics in the paper, even though the main Theorem 1.2 is entirely human. The record's 'none' treats replacing the proof as if it removed the construction too.
